issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows many nullable columns with 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' (e.g. employee.address, employee.city, employee.first_name, employee.last_name, employee.phone, employee.salary, employee.state, employee.title, employee.zip, establishment.address, establishment.dba_name, establishment.state, inspection.inspection_date, inspection.results, inspection_point.*, violation.fine). The NULL rule requires at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance. The cause is in instance.py: `_compact_null_share` returns 0.0 when the compact column has no NULLs, and `fill_foreign_keys_consistently`/samplers then never emit NULL. The clamp `share = min(max(share, 1.0/n), 1.0-1.0/n)` is only applied to FK columns, not to non-FK nullable columns, and even there it is applied only when `n >= 2` and only inside the FK path.
issues.requested_revision: In instance.py, for every nullable non-PK column (not just FK columns), clamp the effective null_share to at least 1/n (and at most 1-1/n) when n >= 2, and force at least one NULL and one non-NULL value per column per instance, mirroring the FK path. This is a non-blocking note per instruction 7 but should be fixed for spec conformance.

issues.evidence: writer.py reports rows_skipped for inspection (109), inspection_point (169), violation (1357) in the aggregate run. These are rows that failed a constraint and were dropped. The spec (instance.py docstring) claims PK/UNIQUE dedup and FK repair happen before insert, so skips indicate residual constraint failures (likely composite PK on violation (inspection_id, point_id) and inspection_point PK collisions, or FK to inspection rows that were themselves skipped).
issues.requested_revision: Investigate and reduce skipped rows: ensure violation's composite PK (inspection_id, point_id) is deduplicated in instance.py (currently only single-column PK and unique_sets are handled; composite PKs are handled by sample_fresh_primary_keys, but violation's PK is composite and the FK repair for inspection_id may reintroduce duplicates after dedup). Also ensure child rows referencing skipped parent rows are not generated. Not blocking since integrity checks pass (0 violations), but the skip counts are high.

issues.evidence: The generation specification is empty (`{}`). The atomic-operation patterns (e.g. comparison_boundary on inspection.inspection_id = 1454071, employee.employee_id = 153225, employee.last_name = 'Rosa', employee.title = 'Sanitarian', establishment.risk_level = 3, inspection.results = 'Pass', LIKE '2010%' on inspection_date, ties_for_order_limit, group_sizes, duplicates_for_distinct) are not explicitly stated as rules. The program implements many of them by construction (fresh keys above compact max, ±1/±2 perturbation, string variants, LIKE patterns, NULL share, tie-capping via max_l0), but the specification does not document these as required rules.
issues.requested_revision: Populate the generation specification with the supported rules: fresh integer keys above compact max for PK/unique ints; ±1/±2 numeric perturbation; string prefix/suffix/drop variants and LIKE patterns without '%'; NULL share following compact share with at least one NULL per nullable column; tie/duplicate capping via max_l0; FK values drawn from compact+generated parent values; composite PK/UNIQUE dedup. Mark uncertain patterns (e.g. exact tie_at_rank=1 for specific columns) as best-effort.

issues.evidence: instance.py `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` is called with `null_share=_compact_null_share(schema, t, tm.columns[0].name)` — it uses the first column's null share for all FK columns of the table, not each FK column's own compact null share. E.g. inspection.license_no and inspection.employee_id get the null share of inspection.inspection_id (a PK, share 0), yet feedback shows inspection.license_no NULL 17/920 and inspection.employee_id NULL 20/920 — these come from the clamp `1/n` applied inside the FK path, not from the column's own share.
issues.requested_revision: Pass each FK column's own compact null share to the FK filler (compute per column inside the loop) rather than the first column's share.

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 349, separated 52. Many atomic-operation patterns (e.g. comparison_boundary on inspection.inspection_id = 1454071 with values [1454070,1454071,1454072], employee.employee_id = 153225, employee.last_name = 'Rosa'/'rosa', employee.title = 'Sanitarian'/'sanitarian'/'SANITARIAN', establishment.risk_level = 3 with [0,1,2,3,4]) are not separated by the generated instances. The program generates fresh keys above compact max (offset), so boundary values like 1454070/1454071/1454072 are never produced; case variants ('Rosa'/'rosa') are not generated by StringSampler (it only adds prefix/suffix/drop, not case changes).
issues.requested_revision: To support comparison_boundary patterns, add case-variant generation in StringSampler (e.g. lower/upper/title variants of compact values) and consider generating integer values near compact boundary values (compact max ± 1) in addition to fresh keys above max. Not blocking per instruction 4 (missing separation alone does not prove error), but improves coverage of the stated patterns.

unresolved_checks: Whether the high rows_skipped counts (inspection 109, inspection_point 169, violation 1357) indicate a systematic composite-PK or FK-repair bug versus expected constraint filtering; integrity checks report 0 violations so this is not blocking.
Whether the empty specification is acceptable given the program implements rules by construction; the designer should document the rules to make the spec non-empty and auditable.
Whether case-variant and boundary-value generation are required by the atomic-operation patterns or are optional best-effort.
